mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, reducing corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 0.5% indicates a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which reduces corporate revenue and profit growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < -0.5% AND HOUST < -0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns; rising employment signals improving consumer confidence and earnings momentum, leading to positive returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly PAYEMS change and subsequent 5-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: During periods when industrial production (INDPRO) is rising while unemployment (UNRATE) is falling, corporate capacity expands without significant labor market slack, boosting profit margins and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0% AND UNRATE < 0% in the same month
regime_hint: supply expansion with labor market tightening
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
